task:B57.title: B57 — the primary and secondary falsifier rule, built, and the harness had no secondary falsifier at all
task:B57.what: Your rule is built. A claim gets a primary tool; a secondary is consulted only where a candidate takes a genuinely different route to the answer, and where none does the primary stands alone AND THE RECORD SAYS SO. The saying-so is the operative half, because an unmarked single-tool verdict reads exactly like a corroborated one. Wolfram is now reachable by the 4 seats that have no shell, through a host-side tool: the remote model asks, this machine evaluates, this machine returns the answer, and no remote model installs anything or touches the licence.
task:B57.why: The rule was already yours and nothing enforced it for 44 days. You ruled on 2026-09-28 that Wolfram is the secondary falsifier run against open-source output and never the primary route. Meanwhile the tool dispatch ended its loop at the first definitive verdict, so it was single-tool by construction and no secondary existed anywhere, for any claim, in any of the 10 subject configurations. Counting tools would not have been enough either: for a statistical claim the 2 candidates both resolved to the identical checking function, so the canonical pair was 1 function called twice.
options: **Leave the secondary pass on by default**, which is my recommendation. An addition nothing reaches is not additive, and a switch exists to turn it off. The cost is 1 extra tool call per definitive verdict, and the Wolfram secondary measures 4.656 seconds against the primary's 0.991, a ratio of 4.700. A record written with the pass switched off still says so, so a skipped pairing can never read as corroborated.

**Allow a disagreeing secondary to change a verdict.** Today it cannot: the disagreement is recorded and the primary stands. My recommendation is to leave it that way until there is a run with disagreements in it to look at, because the alternative changes what the apparatus concludes and I have no measurement to offer yet.

**Leave the 2 software configurations without a secondary.** They are the 3 remaining uncovered pairs. Wolfram cannot decide a control-flow claim and the attempt would cost 4.656 seconds to return nothing, so my recommendation is to leave them and revisit only if a code claim ever needs a second opinion the existing tools cannot give.
